scope: All 7,126 distinct API names in Intel Intrinsics Guide 3.6.9. Every name is assigned exactly one initial work category. Category assignment outside direct source matches is a planning inference and is not an implementation claim.

method.simde_match: A case-sensitive native-alias #define in official SIMDe x86 headers. Definitions are read as source, not presumed available for every compiler/configuration.
method.pure_subset: Only fixed-width scalar/vector/mask inputs and non-void returns; no pointer/array/immediate/system/SVML or unsupported half/BF16 type. Full alias macro expressions are retained.
method.reference_rule: Only actual Intel intrinsic execution counts as Intel evidence. SIMDe, libm, SLEEF, SoftFloat, or a catalog listing cannot be substituted for the Intel reference.
method.group_counts: Work-category counts form a partition; CPUID and technology rows can overlap due to repeated API names and requirement alternatives.
method.integration: src/equilane/simde_codegen.py, contracts/simde-pure-values.json, and vendor/simde contain the initial implementation foundation. Their source-candidate status is distinct from later compile/run evidence.

work_categories.title: AMX state and tile model
work_categories.strategy: Implement per-thread tile configuration/state and tile memory effects, then integer/BF16/FP16 tile kernels. Native Intel evidence needs AMX capability and OS permission; do not substitute a no-op.

work_categories.title: BF16 conversion and dot products
work_categories.strategy: Implement bit-exact BF16 conversion, lane packing, and dot-product accumulation contracts. Do not equate FP32 accumulation with every Intel BF16 rounding or NaN rule.

work_categories.title: Explicit rounding or exception suppression
work_categories.strategy: Generate rounded/SAE adapters with environment save/restore and correctly suppressed exceptions. Removing the round suffix is not a valid implementation.

work_categories.title: FP16 arithmetic and conversion
work_categories.strategy: Use a software IEEE implementation such as Berkeley SoftFloat for half arithmetic, conversions, rounding, and flags, with Intel-specific NaN handling. Verify SIMD packing and masked inactive lanes independently.

work_categories.title: Generated SIMDe / native Intel candidate
work_categories.strategy: Use byte ABI, source-pinned SIMDe body, genuine Intel intrinsic guarded by CPU features, isolated execution, and saved native evidence.

work_categories.title: Masked form of an existing SIMDe kernel
work_categories.strategy: Potentially reuse a base kernel, but evaluate only active lanes when exceptions or memory faults are observable. Masked memory requires per-lane access and guards; blending an eagerly evaluated result is not generally equivalent.

work_categories.title: Existing registered operation
work_categories.strategy: Keep its native evidence and inputs; registration does not imply all-input conformance.

work_categories.title: SIMDe source available; adapter work remains
work_categories.strategy: Extend the signature layer for immediate values, pointers, masks, state, or SVML. Preserve the full macro expression and constant operands.

work_categories.title: Additional vector kernel or alias
work_categories.strategy: Add the exact signature, lane/bit semantics and any alias mapping, implement in portable C or reusable kernels, and independently compare native Intel output.

work_categories.title: Scalar integer or cryptographic kernel
work_categories.strategy: Implement fixed-width C operations with unsigned arithmetic and independent vectors; use dedicated audited crypto primitives where applicable.

work_categories.title: Stateful, system, or platform operation
work_categories.strategy: Specify observable state and capability requirements first. Use an actual OS/hardware operation where meaningful, otherwise report unsupported instead of claiming an equivalent no-op.

work_categories.title: FP16 SVML math
work_categories.strategy: Add half-precision lane conversion and math adapters. Compare against actual Intel compiler/SVML output; scalar libm or SLEEF is a candidate implementation, not an Intel oracle.

reference_gaps: The available Intel/QEMU environment rejects AVX-512 through the CPU guard. Portable AVX-512 execution alone is not equivalence evidence.
SVML needs an Intel compiler/toolchain that supplies the relevant intrinsic declaration and runtime. Standard Clang immintrin.h does not provide that baseline.
System, cache, timing, random, transaction, and AMX operations need explicit observable-state contracts and relevant native capabilities; generated names are insufficient.

sources.role: Pinned portable implementation source; MIT license preserved.
SVML source has scalar math fallbacks and optional SLEEF branches; this does not establish Intel bit equivalence.
Optional vector elementary-function implementation. Current upstream marks RISC-V vector backends unmaintained; four-target support must be independently checked.
Candidate software IEEE arithmetic for half/single/double rounding and exceptions, with per-ISA NaN adaptations still required.
Intel documentation distinguishes SVML library intrinsics from individual CPU instructions and from scalar math accuracy.

recommended_order: Execute and compare the generated pure-value subset under the authenticated byte ABI on all four targets; keep unsupported Intel features explicit.
Expand immediate-aware compilation and pointer/memory schemas, then use the remaining SIMDe aliases with full expressions and no eager evaluation of inactive memory lanes.
Add FP16/BF16 kernels and per-intrinsic rounding/SAE/NaN contracts; independently verify their edge cases.
Add SVML adapters only when a genuine Intel SVML reference toolchain is available; use libm/SLEEF as candidate ports, not expected-output generators.
Add AMX and system-operation state models and native capability tests, keeping model execution and native equivalence results separately labeled.
